Turn your dog into a low-poly 3D model

Walk one slow lap around your dog with your phone. The app cuts the dog out of every shot and builds a game-ready .glb mesh.

    Keep your dog inside the corner frame on screen. The app tracks how far round you are.

Everything runs on your device. Your photos are never uploaded.

Before you start

Pick a clear spot

  • Plain background works best: an empty floor and a wall, or grass. Clutter and other people confuse the cut-out.
  • Soft, even light. Shade outdoors or a bright room. Avoid harsh shadows and backlight.
  • You need to be able to walk a full circle, about 1.5 m (5 ft) from your dog.
🐕 🦴

Settle your dog first

  • Ask for a sit or down + stay and reward with a treat or lick mat, or scan when they're sleepy after a walk.
  • A helper at the dog's head can hold their attention, but stay out of the shot. No hands, legs or leash across the dog.
  • Fidgety dog? Use the Quick lap switch on the camera screen. Fewer photos, faster lap. The app also skips shots where the dog moved.

Walk one slow lap

  • Walk a full circle in about 20 to 30 seconds. Slow and steady, the same distance all the way.
  • Keep the phone at chest height, pointing at the dog.
  • Don't zoom and don't turn the phone sideways mid-lap. The app takes a photo every few degrees and shows your progress.

Frame it right

  • Line the dog up inside the corner frame. All four paws and the tail should stay in view.
  • If the dog is cut off by the screen edge, that shot is skipped.
  • The dog's outline is found automatically. It's easiest when the dog's color contrasts with the background.

Advanced
